sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A lies at the northwest corner of West New York, where Hudson Boulevard West runs diagonally across the page as the boundary between West New York and North Bergen, with the Town of Union boundary along the left edge. The lower part of the sheet is bounded by Bergenline Avenue, with 7th Street running up the page from it to the boulevard and 5th Street entering from the north side of the boulevard. The sheet is mostly open: large undivided tracts, long rows of narrow platted lots with no buildings, and scattered dwellings, sheds and a dance pavilion. The principal works are the Sutro Bros braid factory at the right edge, a large pink-coloured brick complex with an engine and boiler house, a reservoir of 100,000 gallons and a note of its sprinkler and fire-pump equipment; a Public Service Corporation of N.J. transforming station of fireproof construction on the west side of 7th Street; a carriage repository; and a stone crushing yard. A fire alarm box stands on Bergenline Avenue at 7th Street, and at the foot of the sheet a strip of the blocks south of Bergenline Avenue is shown with 5th to 8th Streets. A margin note on the left reads See Volume Eight, and a note at the lower left refers to Volume Eight as well. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right, with Hudson Boulevard West lettered 80 ft wide.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 5th Street is now 49th Street and 7th Street is now 51st Street; Hudson Boulevard West is now John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
The sheet is the northwest corner of the volume; the parts below Bergenline Avenue and beyond the left margin are in Volume Eight.

West New York, 50 ft, NW corner at the North Bergen line; Hudson Blvd West (John F. Kennedy Boulevard) diagonal; old 5th-7th Sts (49th-51st). Sutro Bros note at top right cut out of the mask. Only 4 points (two pairs 100 ft apart along the boulevard): medium-low confidence.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers a strip of central West New York between 13th Street at the foot of the sheet and 17th Street at the top, with Madison Street on the left and Bergenline Avenue down the right side, and Van Buren Place running through the upper half. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. The upper blocks between 16th and 17th Streets are built up with rows of two-storey dwellings, including a long run of buildings lettered Ristow Buildings on Madison Street, and on Van Buren Place and Bergenline Avenue a line of shops with the Town Hall, a fire alarm box, a laundry and an undertaker. Between 15th and 16th Streets the block is lined with flats and shops at the Bergenline Avenue end and with dwellings and a bakery behind them. The lower block between 13th and 15th Streets is largely open lots; it holds the Dodge & Bliss Co. lumber shed and lumber yard, a general machine shop and ironworks near 13th Street, and a few dwellings along Bergenline Avenue. Water pipes of 6 inches and larger run in the streets with hydrants marked, and the cross streets are lettered 40 to 80 ft wide. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins (8, 14, 6, 13, 4). The drawing is at 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 13th to 17th Streets are now 57th to 61st Streets.
Van Buren Place and Madison keep their names today (Van Buren Place, Madison Street).
West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Old 13th-17th Sts (57th-61st), Madison St to Bergenline Av, Van Buren Pl.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A shows the western edge of West New York along Hudson Boulevard West, which crosses the sheet diagonally from upper left to lower right and is lettered as the boundary line between West New York and North Bergen. East of the boulevard the sheet shows the blocks between 13th Street at the top and 9th Street at the foot, divided by Jefferson Street, Adams Street and, at the right edge, Jackson Street. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. Most of the ground is thinly built: long rows of narrow lots on the blocks lettered C and D between 11th and 13th Streets are almost all empty, and the land beside the boulevard is open apart from a wagon shed, an automobile shed and a few dwellings. The built-up part is at the right and bottom: the E. H. Schmidt ice works (manufacturer of ice, with an ice machine, tank room and storage) on the corner of 12th and Jackson Streets, three embroidery factories with electric motors between 10th and 11th Streets, a marble yard and stone cutting works, a greenhouse, saloons and flats, and a church or hall near Arthur Place. Schley Place and Arthur Place are short side streets. Pipes of 6 inches run in the streets and the boulevard is marked as 80 ft wide. Drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 9th to 13th Streets are now 53rd to 57th Streets; Hudson Boulevard West is now John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
Schley Place survives only as a service way in the modern street data.
West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Old 9th-13th Sts (53rd-57th), Hudson Blvd West (Kennedy Blvd) to Jackson St.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers six blocks of central West New York between 13th Street at the top and 9th Street at the bottom, from Jackson Street at the left edge across Polk and Madison Streets to Bergenline Avenue at the right edge. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. Frame dwellings stand on long narrow lots along 13th Street and 10th Street and on the Bergenline Avenue frontage, and the blocks lettered A, B, E and F between 12th and 13th Streets are mostly empty platted lots. The principal works are the Duplan Silk Co. Ida Mill at Jackson Street and 11th Street, with steam heat, electric motors and a watchman, Public School No. 2 with its yard on Polk Street, a button factory and an embroidery factory with electric motor, a bank of flats, hay and wood yards and a wagon painting shop on 10th Street near Bergenline Avenue. Schley Place and Arthur Place are short side streets, Arthur Place running between 10th and 9th Streets. Fire alarm boxes and water pipes of 6 inches are marked in the streets, which are lettered 40 to 80 ft wide. The adjoining sheets are numbered 6, 2, 13, 12, 11 and 1 in the margins. Drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 9th to 13th Streets are now 53rd to 57th Streets.
The Duplan Silk Co. Ida Mill is lettered on the block at Jackson Street and 11th Street.
West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Old 10th-13th Sts (54th-57th), Polk St to Bergenline Av.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A lies along the western boundary of West New York, where Hudson Boulevard West runs down the left side of the page as the line between West New York and North Bergen. East of it the sheet shows the long blocks between 17th Street at the top and 13th Street at the foot, divided by Washington Street, Jefferson Street and Adams Street, with 16th and 15th Streets entering from the right. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. The north end of each block is built with two-storey dwellings, flats and frame stores, including the Liberty Hose Co. No. 1 fire department house on 17th Street, an embroidery factory, a club house, and a contractors yard with lime and lath storage at 16th Street. South of these, the blocks are long narrow lots with only a few buildings, and the lower half of the sheet is a large open tract. On the boulevard frontage there are scattered dwellings, a typewriter shop, and the Madonna Della Libera Roman Catholic Church, with a blacksmith shop near the southern end. Pierce Street and Spring Street are lettered on the left edge. The boulevard is marked 80 ft wide, the cross streets 40 to 50 ft. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the streets. Drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 13th to 17th Streets are now 57th to 61st Streets; Hudson Boulevard West is now John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
The Madonna Della Libera Roman Catholic Church is lettered on the boulevard frontage.
West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Old 13th-17th Sts (57th-61st), Hudson Blvd West to Adams St. 59th St / Kennedy Blvd rejected at 9.3 m (boulevard junction realigned).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A shows central West New York between 17th Street at the top and 13th Street at the foot, with Adams Street at the left edge, Jackson, Polk and Madison Streets across the sheet, and the western edge of the next sheet at the right. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. The upper blocks between 16th and 17th Streets are the most built up: two-storey dwellings, an embroidery works with steam heat and electric light, a metal stamping shop with a stone-melting plant, a tin shop, a wagon shed, a paint shop and the Gethsemane Baptist Church on the block bounded by Polk and Madison Streets. Between 15th and 16th Streets the blocks consist of long narrow lots with a few dwellings and a row of flats. The middle of the sheet, between 15th and 13th Streets, is a large undivided open tract, with a row of dwellings along Madison Street and a line of houses and embroidery works close along 13th Street. The cross streets are lettered 40 to 50 ft wide, with 6 inch water pipes marked, and hydrants and fire alarm boxes are drawn. The neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins (7, 8, 5, 2, 3 and 4). Drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 13th to 17th Streets are now 57th to 61st Streets.
The Gethsemane Baptist Church is lettered on the block between Polk and Madison Streets.
West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Old 13th-17th Sts (57th-61st), Adams St to Madison St.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A shows the northwest corner of West New York, where the town meets North Bergen along Hudson Boulevard West. The sheet is bounded by 17th Street at the bottom and 21st Street at the top, with Washington Street at the left and Jackson Street at the right; Jefferson Street and Adams Street run up the page between them, and 18th Street cuts across the middle. Hudson Boulevard West crosses the upper left as a diagonal, and the lettered boundary between North Bergen and West New York runs along it, with a 6 inch water pipe beside the line. Blocks below 18th Street are filled with lots of about 25 ft, mostly two-storey frame and brick dwellings, with sheds, a bowling alley with a saloon, a hall, a hay and feed store and a tin smith's shop among them. Trinity Reformed Church stands on Adams Street at 17th Street with a temporary annex to the school beside it. The blocks above 18th Street are larger and more thinly built, with scattered dwellings and several vacant lots. The Gerretson Silk Co. works, with its own electric plant, fire pump and heating, stand at the head of the Jefferson to Adams block on 21st Street. Streets of 40, 50 and 80 ft are lettered. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and is turned so that, from the fitted placement, north lies toward the upper left; the compass sits in the upper left, next to Bergenwood Avenue and South Street, which are only sketched at the edge of the drawn area.
notes: Old 17th, 18th and 21st Streets are 61st, 62nd and 65th Streets today.
Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
The rotation fitted from the control points is about -31 degrees; the printed compass was not used to check this.

West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Old 17th-21st Sts (61st-65th), Washington to Jackson Sts; Hudson Blvd West and the North Bergen line at upper left (Bergenwood Av, South St, Robert St lettered in North Bergen).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers a block-wide strip of West New York between 17th Street at the bottom and 21st Street at the top, from Jackson Street at the left edge to Bergenline Avenue at the right. Polk Street and Madison Street cross the sheet, both with a visible jog at 18th Street, and Van Buren Place runs up the lower right. The district is built-up residential: two-storey frame and brick dwellings on lots of about 25 ft, with sheds and stables behind, and a good many vacant lots in the upper blocks between 18th and 21st Streets. Embroidery works stand in the blocks near 20th Street and Polk Street, and an embroidery works and a flats building occupy the block near Jackson Street at the upper left. District School No. 10, a large brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, with a bell tower and a kindergarten beside it, stands in the block between Polk and Madison Streets just below 18th Street. In the lower blocks are the Excelsior Fire Engine Co. house of the fire department, a hall and a stone yard near 17th Street. Bergenline Avenue at the right edge carries the commercial frontage, with shops and a stable; at the upper right is a wood sawing works. Water pipes of 6 inches and street widths of 33, 38 and 40 ft are lettered. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and is turned so that, from the fitted placement, north lies toward the upper left; the compass is near the top margin.
notes: Old 17th, 18th, 20th and 21st Streets are 61st, 62nd, 64th and 65th Streets today.
Polk and Madison Streets are drawn with a jog at 18th Street; the modern junction with 62nd Street has two nodes there.
The detector rejected 62nd Street / Polk Street (10.9 m) because of this jog.
West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Old 17th-21st Sts (61st-65th), Jackson St to Bergenline Av; Polk and Madison jog at 18th St (both modern nodes used).

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 9 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A is the West New York half of the sheet lettered 'West New York & Guttenberg'. It runs from Hudson Boulevard West and the lettered North Bergen boundary line at the top down to Bergenline Avenue at the bottom, and from 21st Street at the left edge to the dash-dot West New York and Guttenberg boundary line on the right. 22nd Street and 23rd Street run up the page; Jackson, Polk and Madison Streets cross them. Streets here are lettered 40 and 50 ft wide, but Jackson Street between 21st and 22nd Streets is drawn only about 27 ft. The upper left block is a large tract cut into long narrow lots, almost all vacant. The block between 22nd and 23rd Streets holds a line of small dwellings and a few shops, a fire department building, a bakery, bowling alleys and, near the top, Duhne's Hotel with its hall, stage and open shed. The next block to the left contains the Church & School of Our Lady Help of Christians, with St. Mary's Hall. Below Polk the blocks are lined with two-storey dwellings with bay fronts, an embroidery works, the Hudson Boulevard Embroidery Wks. at the upper right near 23rd Street, and a row of brick stores on Bergenline Avenue at the bottom edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right; the compass is in the left block. Adjoining sheets are numbered 7, 8, 5, 6, 16 and 33 in the margins, and the Guttenberg half of the sheet is part 2.
notes: Old 21st, 22nd and 23rd Streets are 65th, 66th and 67th Streets today.
Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.
Polk Street is drawn with a jog at 23rd Street, where it meets the Guttenberg grid; modern 67th Street / Polk Street was rejected (10 m).
Only six control points, all in the left two thirds of the part; medium to low confidence.

Lettered West New York & Guttenberg, 50 ft. Two parts: 1, West New York west of the dash-dot town line (old 21st-23rd Sts = 65th-67th); 2, Guttenberg east of it (Adams, Jackson, Polk, Madison = Guttenberg 8th-5th Sts; 24th St (Hudson Av) = 68th St), a helmert on four hand-picked points along 68th St (the detector paired a lot line 13 m inside the block; hand-picked as the drawn block edge plus 25 ft).

sheet-9-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 9 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A is the Guttenberg half of the sheet lettered 'West New York & Guttenberg'. It lies east of the dash-dot boundary line lettered 'West New York' and 'Guttenberg', and is bounded on the right by 24th Street (Hudson Avenue) and at the top by Hudson Boulevard West, where the North Bergen boundary line is lettered. Four Guttenberg cross streets, Adams (8th Street), Jackson (7th Street), Polk (6th Street) and Madison (5th Street), run across it, each drawn about 50 ft between lots numbered in even and odd series. The blocks hold mostly two-storey dwellings and flats on narrow lots, with an embroidery works and wagon sheds, bowling alleys, a carpenter shop and a tin shop in the Jackson to Polk block, and further embroidery works with power, steam heat and lights at the top, one of them lettered F. Fuchs, Swiss Embroidery. The lower blocks below Madison Street are thinly built, with the bottom edge running to Park Avenue. Several blocks, including the one at the lower right, are drawn with vacant lots. The part is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Only the Hudson Avenue street line carries control, so placement rests on a single street.
notes: Guttenberg's 8th, 7th, 6th and 5th Streets are Adams, Jackson, Polk and Madison Streets today, and Hudson Avenue (24th Street) is 68th Street.
Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard today.

Placed as a helmert from four hand-picked points along 24th Street (68th Street), the street cut by the sheet edge (drawn block edge plus 25 ft); the detector had paired a lot line 13 m inside the block. Low confidence.

Lettered West New York & Guttenberg, 50 ft. Two parts: 1, West New York west of the dash-dot town line (old 21st-23rd Sts = 65th-67th); 2, Guttenberg east of it (Adams, Jackson, Polk, Madison = Guttenberg 8th-5th Sts; 24th St (Hudson Av) = 68th St), a helmert on four hand-picked points along 68th St (the detector paired a lot line 13 m inside the block; hand-picked as the drawn block edge plus 25 ft).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A shows a long wedge of the southern edge of West New York between Bulls Ferry Road on the west and Hudson Boulevard East on the east, from the sheet's north end down to 7th Street, which lies on the Weehawken boundary. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. Fairview Terrace runs down the middle between the two roads, joining 10th Street near the top and ending at 7th Street, and Hudson Boulevard East curves to the right, with the heavy line of its far side drawn as an arc. The built blocks are small: a single row of two-and-a-half storey dwellings stands along the west side of Fairview Terrace, and on the east side a close row of brick houses with bay fronts runs along Hudson Boulevard East; a church or chapel and a few other dwellings lie farther south. Many lots are drawn but empty. Above 10th Street the blocks are outlined for subdivision, with two flats and a few lots built. Outside the mask the sheet shows only the outlines of blocks on neighbouring sheets, stubs of 8th, 9th and 11th Streets, and a match line lettered A and B near the top. The area below 7th Street is marked 'See Volume Eight'. Street widths of 50, 60 and 80 feet and 6 inch water pipes are marked. The scale is 50 ft to an inch.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th Streets are now 51st to 55th Streets.
Bulls Ferry Road is today's Park Avenue and Hudson Boulevard East is today's Boulevard East.

Placed from four points on the Fairview Terrace and Boulevard East junctions, two of them hand-picked at 7th Street; Bulls Ferry Road was left out of the fit because including it changed the scale by 3 to 4 percent.

West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Wedge between Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av) and Hudson Blvd East (Boulevard East), old 7th-11th Sts (51st-55th), Weehawken line at the bottom ('See Volume Eight'). 2 detected and 2 hand-picked points (7th St row); Bulls Ferry Rd left out (shifted scale 3-4 percent).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers the western edge of West New York, from Bergenline Avenue at the top of the sheet to Hudson Avenue at the bottom, with Palisade Avenue crossing the middle. Three north-south streets, 6th, 7th and 8th Streets, divide the sheet into blocks, and a strip along the left edge is lettered as the boundary line between West New York and the Town of Union (marked as the proposed and present line), beside the adjoining sheet of another volume. The upper blocks between Bergenline and Palisade Avenues are partly built with two-storey frame dwellings, stores and sheds, and mostly divided into lots. Named buildings include the Enterprise Hose Co. No. 3 fire department house on 7th Street, a mineral water factory with engine and boiler near 6th and 7th Streets, and a decorative glass works close to the boundary line. A row of dwellings stands on the east side of 8th Street, with more along 6th Street at the lower left. South of Palisade Avenue a large block between 7th and 8th Streets is drawn as one undivided plot, with slate cutting works on the 6th Street side and a few scattered dwellings. The streets north of Bergenline Avenue are offset to the west of those south of it, and the sheet notes 50, 60 and 80 foot widths. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, as the compass at the top shows.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 6th, 7th and 8th Streets are now 50th, 51st and 52nd Streets.
Bergenline Avenue is crossed by streets that jog: the modern street grid north of it is offset from the south side, giving two modern junction nodes for 51st Street.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 6th-8th Sts (50th-52nd), Bergenline Av to Hudson Av; streets jog at Bergenline Av.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A shows a band of West New York between Bergenline Avenue at the top and Hudson Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Palisade Avenue, and running from 9th Street at the left to 12th Street at the right edge. North of Palisade Avenue the blocks are partly built. 10th Street and Garfield Place carry most of the dwellings, many of them two-storey, with a larger group of frame houses and stores along the north side of Grant Place and Gaw Place at the right. Industry is concentrated in the middle: the Neuburger Embroidery Works with its electric power plant at the foot of 10th Street, the Novelty Web Co. on Garfield Place, a second embroidery works, and the Ideal Steam Laundry with a stable and stone yard beside Gaw Place. Two blue-tinted buildings north of Garfield Place are marked as artificial stone works. South of Palisade Avenue the blocks between 9th, 10th, 11th and 12th Streets are laid out in narrow lots and almost unbuilt, apart from a United Presbyterian Church and a carpenter's shop near Hudson Avenue and a few flats at the lower left corner. A compass near the middle shows north to the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, with 6 inch water pipes lettered in the streets and street widths of 35 to 60 feet noted at block corners.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 9th to 12th Streets are now 53rd to 56th Streets.
Garfield Place north of Palisade Avenue lies on the line of 11th Street (modern 55th Street); 11th Street is lettered both above Bergenline Avenue and below Palisade Avenue.

Streets north of Bergenline Avenue are offset from those south of it, so junctions on Bergenline Avenue are measured on the north arm of the cross street and fit less tightly (53rd Street junction about 3.5 m).
Schley Place is only a service way in modern data and was not used as control.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 9th-11th Sts (53rd-55th), Bergenline Av to Hudson Av.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A shows six blocks of central West New York, in two rows of three, between 12th Street at the west side of the sheet and 15th Street at the east side. Bergenline Avenue, the commercial street, runs along the top of the sheet, Palisade Avenue crosses the middle and Hudson Avenue lies along the bottom; 13th and 14th Streets divide the blocks. Grant Place and Gaw Place enter from the left edge, west of 12th Street. The district is residential, built over with two-storey frame and brick dwellings on narrow lots, many drawn in long uniform rows, with large stretches of vacant lots, especially in the lower blocks. A bakery and a laundry stand on Bergenline Avenue at 13th Street, shops and stores line the avenue at 12th and 15th Streets, and a row of flats with party walls occupies the south end of the block between 12th and 13th Streets on Hudson Avenue. A small concrete embroidery works with electric power stands in the block between 13th and 14th Streets below Palisade Avenue. A frame wooden shed is lettered on Bergenline Avenue near 15th Street. Water pipes of 6 to 30 inches are marked in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes, and widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered at block corners. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right, and block numbers 1 to 3 are printed in the blocks.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 12th to 15th Streets are now 56th to 59th Streets.
Grant Place and Gaw Place are shown only as stubs at the west edge of the sheet.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 12th-15th Sts (56th-59th), Bergenline Av to Hudson Av; Grant Pl and Gaw Pl stubs at the left.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers three blocks of central West New York between 15th Street on the west edge and 17th Street on the east edge, running from Bergenline Avenue at the top of the sheet down to Hudson Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Harrison Place, Tyler Place, Palisade Avenue and Monroe Place. 16th Street divides the sheet. The district is residential and largely built on narrow 25 ft lots, many of them still vacant in 1910. Two-storey frame and brick dwellings line the streets, with long uniform rows of two-storey brick dwellings with bay fronts on the north side of Palisade Avenue and on the south side of Tyler Place between 16th and 17th Streets. Shops, saloons and an insurance office front Bergenline Avenue, the commercial street. Named buildings include the Empire Hook and Ladder Company No. 2 fire house on Bergenline Avenue at 15th Street, the West New York Athletic Club on Harrison Place near 17th Street, the Trinity Reformed Church (drawn from plans) at 15th Street and Palisade Avenue, and William Spiess's embroidery factory with an electric motor house on Monroe Place, next to a wood yard at 17th Street and Hudson Avenue. Water pipes of 6 to 36 inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right; street widths of 50 to 80 ft are lettered at the block corners.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 15th, 16th and 17th Streets are now 59th, 60th and 61st Streets.
Trinity Reformed Church is drawn from plans, not yet built in 1910.
West New York, 50 ft. Bergenline Av to Hudson Av between 15th and 17th Sts (modern 59th-61st), Harrison, Tyler, Monroe Pls. Pilot sheet: 14 auto GCPs, ink_below_paper 80.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers eight blocks of central West New York between 17th Street at the west edge and a line just beyond 19th Street at the east edge, from Bergenline Avenue at the top to Hudson Avenue at the bottom. Harrison Place, Tyler Place, Palisade Avenue and Monroe Place cross the sheet, and 18th Street divides the two columns of blocks. The west column is mostly small dwellings on 25 ft lots, with a few brick rows, flats and a shop on Palisade Avenue. The east column is more open, with many vacant lots and scattered dwellings, and its blocks are broken by an unnamed alley and lot lines that do not follow the street grid. Industry is a feature of the sheet. The Hudson Silk Company stands on Harrison Place near 18th Street, with watchman's clock stations, steam heat and electric light. The Phoenix Embroidery Works and the St. Gall Embroidery Works occupy the east blocks above Palisade Avenue, and Rogers and Thompson's silk mill, a long brick building, stands on Monroe Place at 19th Street. A machine shop and embroidery works, a wood yard, a club house and a church are shown. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right, and block numbers 2 to 10 are printed in the blocks. Water pipes are marked in the avenues.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 17th, 18th and 19th Streets are now 61st, 62nd and 63rd Streets.
Rogers and Thompson's silk mill is lettered on both this sheet and sheet 16.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 17th-19th Sts (61st-63rd), Bergenline Av to Hudson Av, Harrison, Tyler, Monroe Pls.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers the blocks of central West New York between 20th Street at the west and 23rd Street at the east, from Bergenline Avenue at the top to Hudson Avenue at the bottom, with Palisade Avenue across the middle; 21st and 22nd Streets divide the blocks. The sheet is mainly residential, with frame and brick two- and three-storey dwellings and flats on narrow lots, closely built along the upper blocks and more openly below Palisade Avenue. Institutional buildings are prominent: St. Joseph's R.C. Church, with its rectory, and St. Joseph's School (marked as drawn from plans) stand above Palisade Avenue on 20th Street; St. John's German Lutheran Church and its pastor's house are on Bergenline Avenue at 21st Street; and Public School No. 4, a large brick building with direct and indirect heating and electric lighting, stands below Palisade Avenue between 21st and 22nd Streets. St. Joseph's Church has a club house on the lower block at 20th Street. Rogers and Thompson's silk mill, a long brick weaving and finishing works, stands on the south side of Palisade Avenue at 22nd Street, with a drying shop and oil storage beside it. An embroidery works and a manufactory of firemen's hats are lettered in the upper east block, where several foundations are drawn. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right, and a north arrow stands in the lower middle.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 20th to 23rd Streets are now 64th to 67th Streets.
St. Joseph's School is lettered 'From Plans' and was not yet built in 1910.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 20th-23rd Sts (64th-67th), Bergenline Av to Hudson Av; St Joseph's church and school, Rogers & Thompson silk mill.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A shows the southern edge of West New York at the Weehawken line, between Hudson Avenue at the top and Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom, with Broadway across the middle. 6th, 7th and 8th Streets divide the blocks; the map is cut on the left by a dash-dot boundary line lettered as the line between Union and West New York, and the adjoining area is marked to be seen in volume eight. The upper blocks, between Hudson Avenue and Broadway, hold close rows of two-storey frame dwellings on 25 ft lots, with a street railway right of way running across the sheet between the two avenues. Between Broadway and Bulls Ferry Road the blocks are only partly built: flats and dwellings stand near 6th Street and Bulls Ferry Road, a contractor's wire shop and sheds stand at 7th Street, and large parts of the blocks are vacant. Bulls Ferry Road runs diagonally across the bottom of the sheet and is itself the boundary with Weehawken; the blocks south of it, including a continuation of 5th, 6th and 7th Streets, are outlined only and are drawn on another volume. Street widths of 50, 60 and 80 feet and water pipes are lettered. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, with north to the upper right.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 6th, 7th and 8th Streets are now 50th, 51st and 52nd Streets.
Bulls Ferry Road is today's Park Avenue; it was left out of the georeferencing because OpenStreetMap shows it as two stretches side by side and the 50th Street junction fell 26 m from the fit.
The vertical dash-dot line at the left edge is lettered as the boundary line between Union (today Union City) and West New York.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 6th-8th Sts (50th-52nd), Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av) at the Weehawken line; Union boundary at the left; Bulls Ferry Rd left out of the fit.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A lies in southern West New York, between Hudson Avenue at the top and Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom, with Broadway crossing the middle. Four north-south streets, 9th, 10th, 11th and 12th Streets, bound three full blocks across the sheet. The land is almost entirely laid out in lots but unbuilt: only a handful of buildings are drawn, among them a row of six two-storey flats on the east side of 10th Street below Broadway, a saloon and shed beside Bulls Ferry Road, an embroidery factory with electric motor and four dwellings on the south side of Hudson Avenue, and a furnishing shop at the right. A strip lettered Street Railway Right of Way runs below Hudson Avenue between the first and second rows of blocks. Bulls Ferry Road runs diagonally across the bottom of the sheet, slanting relative to the grid, so the blocks along it are cut at an angle. The compass at the top right shows north to the upper right, and the sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Street widths of 50, 60 and 80 feet and 6, 16 and 30 inch water pipes are lettered along the streets. Adjoining sheets 12, 17, 19 and 10 are named in the margins.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 9th to 12th Streets are now 53rd to 56th Streets.
Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue.
56th Street / Hudson Avenue was detected 12.9 m from the fit and rejected; the junction lies at the right edge of the sheet.
West New York, 50 ft. Southern blocks, old 9th-12th Sts (53rd-56th), Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A continues the southern part of West New York east of sheet 18, from Hudson Avenue at the top to Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom, with Broadway across the middle. The streets that cross the sheet are 12th, 13th, 14th and 15th Streets, and Buchanan Place runs off 14th Street into the lower right block. As on sheet 18 the blocks are divided into narrow lots and mostly empty. Building is limited to the right-hand blocks: a pink-tinted row of brick stores and dwellings at the top right corner by a fire alarm box on Hudson Avenue, a row of two-storey frame dwellings with a flat on the east side of 15th Street above Broadway, and below Broadway more dwellings and several three-storey flats on 15th Street, with an auto shed and a brick building beside Buchanan Place. A Street Railway Right of Way is lettered under the first row of blocks beneath Hudson Avenue. Bulls Ferry Road crosses the foot of the sheet at a slant, giving the lowest blocks sloped bases. A compass at the lower left shows north to the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, with 50 and 60 foot street widths and 6, 16 and 30 inch water pipes marked.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 12th to 15th Streets are now 56th to 59th Streets.
Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue.
Buchanan Place was not listed in the config streets and is not used as control.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 12th-15th Sts (56th-59th), Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av).

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers a strip of West New York between 15th Street at the west edge and 17th Street at the east edge, running from Hudson Avenue at the top of the sheet down to Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom. 16th Street divides it. Fillmore Place, Broadway, Buchanan Place and, in the lower right block, Westover Place cross or serve the blocks. A block-wide strip between Hudson Avenue and Fillmore Place is lettered as a street railway right of way and is left as a long empty tract of lots. Most of the sheet is divided into narrow 25 ft lots, the greater part of them still vacant in 1910. Building is concentrated along 15th Street and 16th Street in the west blocks, where rows of two-storey dwellings and a few brick houses stand, and in the blocks east of 16th Street around Fillmore Place and Broadway, where frame dwellings, stables and small sheds are scattered. A public school with pink brick walls stands on Broadway near 17th Street. Further dwellings and outbuildings fill the blocks around Westover Place near the bottom right. Bulls Ferry Road, the old road along the foot of the sheet, runs obliquely and cuts off the bottom row of blocks as irregular lots. Street widths of 50 and 80 ft are lettered at the corners. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north toward the upper right, and carries a compass at the upper right and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 15th, 16th and 17th Streets are now 59th, 60th and 61st Streets.
Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue.
Hudson Avenue is printed 'Hudson Av.'; the street railway right of way strip between Hudson Avenue and Fillmore Place is lettered as a note, not a named street.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 15th-17th Sts (59th-61st), Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av).

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers the blocks of West New York between 17th Street at the west edge and 19th Street near the east edge, from Hudson Avenue at the top to Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom. 18th Street runs down the middle of the sheet. Dewey Avenue crosses at the upper right, with Fillmore Place, Broadway, Buchanan Place and Johnson Place crossing the blocks in order down the page. A street railway right of way is lettered across the strip of lots between Hudson Avenue and Fillmore Place, as on the adjoining sheet. The blocks are cut into narrow 25 ft lots and most are vacant. Building is clustered near the west edge, along 17th Street, where rows of two-storey frame dwellings, flats and stores stand beside a pink brick building at Broadway, and on the blocks around Fillmore Place and Buchanan Place, where dwellings and outbuildings are scattered. A long narrow building stands on the east side of 18th Street between Fillmore Place and Broadway. At the lower left a row of attached dwellings fronts Bulls Ferry Road, which crosses the foot of the sheet at a slant. A pink building and a small blue-coloured structure stand at 19th Street and Broadway near the east edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north toward the upper right; the compass is at the upper right and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 17th, 18th and 19th Streets are now 61st, 62nd and 63rd Streets.
Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue.
Dewey Avenue and Hudson Avenue are printed 'Dewey Av.' and 'Hudson Av.'.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 17th-19th Sts (61st-63rd), Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av).

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A covers the eastern blocks of West New York, from Hudson Avenue at the top to Bulls Ferry Road at the bottom and from 20th Street near the west edge to 23rd Street at the east edge, with 21st Street and 22nd Street between. Dewey Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet and bends at the upper right where a diagonal line, apparently the line of a road or right of way, cuts across the blocks toward the lower right. Broadway crosses the middle. The ground is almost entirely subdivided into narrow lots and almost entirely vacant in 1910. The only buildings are a few dwellings and sheds on the blocks between Hudson Avenue and Dewey Avenue, a pink-coloured building near 21st Street, a small cluster of outbuildings at the centre, and one small building at the foot of the sheet near Bulls Ferry Road. The lower two thirds of the sheet is a regular grid of blank lot lines on the blocks between Broadway and Bulls Ferry Road. Block numbers are lettered in the centre of each block. Bulls Ferry Road runs along the bottom edge with the scale bar below it. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north toward the upper right; a compass appears at the upper left.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 20th, 21st, 22nd and 23rd Streets are now 64th, 65th, 66th and 67th Streets.
Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue.
Hudson Avenue and Dewey Avenue are printed 'Hudson Av.' and 'Dewey Av.'.
The diagonal line at the upper right was not identified on the sheet; it may be a proposed road.
West New York, 50 ft. Old 20th-23rd Sts (64th-67th), mostly vacant lots, Hudson Av to Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av).

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 of the 1910 Hudson County volume 8A is mostly blank paper. Only a strip at the top is built up: two blocks of West New York along 23rd Street, between Bulls Ferry Road at the west edge and the curving line of Hudson Boulevard East at the right, separated by Lincoln Place and McKinley Place. The blocks hold two-storey frame dwellings, some of them flats, standing in rows along the west side of each place, with outbuildings and sheds behind. Lot numbers and street widths of 50 ft are lettered at the corners; Bulls Ferry Road is lettered 80 ft wide. Below the second row of blocks the sheet is drawn only as an empty tract with no streets or lots, crossed by a dash-dot match line lettered A near the bottom. A compass with its north arrow pointing to the upper left stands in the blank area, so the sheet is turned about 90 degrees from its neighbours: Bulls Ferry Road runs up the page on the left and Hudson Boulevard East curves along the right edge. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, with the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Old West New York street numbers are 44 lower than today's: 23rd Street is now 67th Street.
Bulls Ferry Road is now Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is now Boulevard East.
Hudson Boulevard East is printed 'Hudson B'l'v'd East'.

Only 67th Street / Lincoln Place and McKinley Place are drawn in full; the 66th Street junctions with Lincoln and McKinley Place and the Park Avenue junction are hand-picked from the drawn block edges (low confidence).

West New York, 50 ft, turned (north to upper left). Blocks on old 23rd St (67th) between Lincoln and McKinley Pls, rest a blank tract; old 22nd St (66th) not drawn. 2 detected and 3 hand-picked points (drawn edge plus half width): medium-low confidence.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers a large, almost empty tract on the Palisades in the north-east of West New York, between Bulls Ferry Road along the west edge of the sheet and Hudson Boulevard East along the edge of the cliff on the east. 16th Street and the head of New Ferry Road (Hillside Road) cross the bottom of the sheet. Hudson Boulevard East, lettered 80 ft wide and 100 ft wide on its northern stretch, enters from the top right, turns west across the middle of the sheet and turns south again to meet 16th Street and New Ferry Road, which descends the cliff towards the West Shore Railroad terminal drawn on sheet 28. The land between Bulls Ferry Road and the boulevard is drawn only as two large unbuilt parcels divided by a property line and a dash-dot match line lettered A and B; no buildings stand on it. The only buildings are at the lower left, on the east side of Bulls Ferry Road just north of 16th Street: a store and dwelling with a wagon shed and a small outbuilding, beside a row of lots that continue on sheet 21. A 16 inch water pipe runs in Bulls Ferry Road. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, unlike most sheets of the volume, so that Bulls Ferry Road runs up the page. Reference numbers in the margins point to sheets 20, 21, 23, 27 and 28.
notes: Bulls Ferry Road here is today's Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East; 16th Street is 60th Street; New Ferry Road (Hillside Road) is Hillside Road.

Placed from only two street junctions (60th Street at Park Avenue and at Boulevard East and Hillside Road), about 75 m apart; the far corners of the sheet rest on the atlas scale and that short baseline.
The 1910 boulevard's turn east of Monitor Place is drawn about 40 m longer than modern Boulevard East's; the modern road has probably been re-cut here.

West New York, 50 ft, turned (north upper left). Almost empty tract between Bulls Ferry Rd (Park Av) and Hudson Blvd East (Boulevard East), 16th St (60th) at bottom. Helmert from two junctions on 60th St; low confidence.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 shows the Hudson River waterfront at the northern edge of West New York, below the Palisades, at the boundary with Guttenberg. Across the top run Farragut Place and the Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, with 27th Street (Ferry Road) on the right edge, where the West New York and Guttenberg boundary line follows its west side. New Ferry Road (Hillside Road) curves down the cliff from the south-west to the turnpike, and a second New Ferry Road crosses the sheet below the railroad tracks. The north end of the West Shore Railroad yard runs across the sheet, with the property line between the West Shore Railroad and the New York, Ontario and Western Railroad. The waterfront is taken up by the New York, Ontario and Western Railroad coal docks, two long trestle piers on piles carrying tracks and hydrants, with the H. L. Herbert and Co. coal office and store, a boiler and engine house under the trestle, and the large works of the American Cotton Oil Company (The W. J. Wilcox Lard and Refining Co.): brick buildings for storage, shipping and packing, lard rolling, oleo storage and soap powder manufacturing (Gold Dust), a soap house, boiler house, iron-clad buildings, cotton oil tanks on the hill lettered A to K with capacities of 1,500 to 7,500 barrels, and a refrigerating, storage, printing and cooperage building on its own pier. A long printed note describes the company's construction, sprinkler system and fire protection. Saloons and a lumber shed and machine shop stand along the turnpike. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north to the upper right.
notes: 27th Street (Ferry Road) is today's Ferry Road; the Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike is probably today's River Road. The waterfront has been rebuilt (Port Imperial).

Placed from one corner of the turnpike and the 40 ft road that sheet 27 also draws, with the atlas scale and an assumed north of 55 degrees; three other shared corners agree within 2 m. The 1910 junction of 27th Street and the turnpike then lies about 40 m from the modern Ferry Road and River Road junction, so one of the two has moved; the sheet is low confidence.
The American Cotton Oil Company's printed note at the lower right is cut out of the mask.
Initials and the date April 1910 are written at the lower right.

West New York waterfront at the Guttenberg line, 50 ft. NYO&W coal docks, American Cotton Oil Co (Wilcox lard works), Hoboken & Hudson River Turnpike, Farragut Pl, 27th St (Ferry Rd). Printed note notched out of the mask. Placed from a corner shared with sheet 27 plus atlas scale and assumed north; low confidence.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the Hudson River shore of West New York below the Palisades, between the West Shore Railroad yards of sheet 28 to the south and the coal docks of sheet 25 to the north. Hudson Boulevard East follows the top of the cliff along the west edge of the sheet, with 23rd Street meeting it at the top left; below the cliff New Ferry Road (Hillside Road) curves north along the foot of the slope to the Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, and a second New Ferry Road runs north beside the tracks. The middle of the sheet is filled by the main tracks of the West Shore Railroad Terminals (New York Central and Hudson River Railroad), fanning into Yard No. 8, with lumber sheds, a steel storage building, storage sheds and the railroad's marine shops, which carry a printed note on their watchmen, lighting and salt-water fire service. On the waterfront are Pier No. 12, Pier No. 13 and Pier No. 15, all on piles, a proposed pier, a dredged channel, and the West Shore ferry house at Pier No. 15 with the ferry to 42nd Street, New York. North of the property line between the New York, Ontario and Western Railroad and the West Shore Railroad lie the New York, Ontario and Western coal docks, drawn in full on sheet 25. Filling lines and the pier line approved by the Secretary of War on May 18th 1897 are drawn in the river. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left and the shore runs up the page.
notes: 23rd Street is today's 67th Street; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East.

The yards, piers and shore have been entirely rebuilt (Port Imperial). The sheet is placed from two points of the A-B match line it shares with sheet 28 and a hand-picked 67th Street / Boulevard East junction; the three agree within about 1.5 m under a similarity fit, but the match line itself rests on sheet 28's extrapolation from its top strip.
Ferry to 42nd Street, New York, from the West Shore ferry house at Pier No. 15.

West New York waterfront, 100 ft, turned (north upper left). West Shore RR terminal tracks, piers 12, 13, 15, ferry house, marine shops; Hudson Blvd East along the cliff. Placed from the A-B match line shared with sheet 28 and 67th St / Boulevard East; low confidence.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, shows the northern part of the West Shore Railroad terminal yards (New York Central and Hudson River Railroad) on the Hudson River shore below the Palisades, at the foot of West New York. Along the top of the sheet runs the edge of the town on the cliff: Bulls Ferry Road, 13th Street and 16th Street, Hudson Boulevard East along the brow of the cliff, and New Ferry Road (Hillside Road) descending the cliff face from 16th Street and curving north towards the ferry. Below the cliff the sheet is filled by the fan of yard tracks, lettered Yard No. 1 to No. 8 with Yard No. 6A, converging eastward towards the main line. The West Shore Railroad power station, a fire-proof generating plant with condenser pumps, generators and two salt-water pumps supplying light and power to the stations and yard, stands at the upper left beside a water tank and boilers, with a few small railroad buildings nearby. On the waterfront are Pier No. 11 on piles carrying tracks, two proposed piers, the float bridge hoist with transfer bridge slips No. 5 and No. 6, and a dredged channel; the exterior line for solid filling and the exterior line for piers approved by the Secretary of War on May 18th 1897 are drawn across the river. Water pipes of 6 to 14 inches, including a salt water system then under construction and the Hackensack Water Company's main, are marked with hose houses and hydrants. The sheet is turned with north to the upper right.
notes: 13th and 16th Streets are today's 57th and 60th Streets; Bulls Ferry Road is Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East.

The yards, piers and shore have been entirely rebuilt (Port Imperial); the sheet is placed only from the street strip along its top edge (two junctions, one hand-picked boundary junction and one modern street line extended 72 m), so the waterfront 300 to 700 m away rests on extrapolation.
Exterior line for piers approved by the Secretary of War, May 18th 1897.

West New York waterfront, 100 ft. West Shore RR (NYC&HR) yards 1-8, power station, pier 11, float bridge; top strip Bulls Ferry Rd, 13th and 16th Sts, Hudson Blvd East, New Ferry Rd (Hillside Rd). Placed from the top strip only; yards extrapolated; low confidence.
